strategy.title: Sell nine $1,500 done-for-you small-business websites by cold email, built by a marketplace junior designer and paid by buyer deposits

stop: Fewer than 2 paid deposits from the first 1,000 contacts by day 10 (including exactly 1): stop outreach; any deposit already taken is fulfilled and its balance collected
Fewer than 3 designers quoting at or below $600 with 2-build capacity by day 10: stop taking new deposits beyond what quoted capacity can deliver within 15 days

continue: 2 or more deposits and a quote at or below $600 by day 10: email the remaining 4,000 contacts by day 20 and close to 10 builds by day 26

answers.resolution: ACCEPTED. answers.resolution: ACCEPTED. $1,800 advanced for builds 1-3 on days 8, 10, 12; owner outlay $2,044 within $2,500.

answers.finding: Offer text must state the real delivery time
answers.resolution: ACCEPTED. The offer as sent promises live within 15 days of the deposit (the longest wait in this schedule, build 4: deposit day 14, live day 29); builds 1-3 go live in 7 days. The card's 'live in 7 days' wording is the route as admitted, not the offer sent.

answers.resolution: ACCEPTED and stated in validation.proof.

reviews.reasons: The shape (cold-email test, deposit-funded subcontracted builds, $94 at risk inside the $2,500 cap) is reasonable, but the plan does not reach the target on its own ledger and its test cannot decide it. (1) Settlement: build 8's balance is received day 42 and settles day 46, build 9's is received day 45 and settles day 49 - both outside the 45-day window, contradicting the SETTLES_IN_TIME disagreement's 'last balance day 39'. Settled in the window: 9 deposits x $750 + 7 balances x $750 = $12,000 gross, and Stripe payouts are net of fees (~$43.80 per build on two charges), so settled cash is below $12,000. If 'cash in the bank' is read as net of the owner's costs, it is ~$7,600 ($13,500 - $5,400 designers - $394 Stripe - $94 Instantly), far short. (2) Volume vs channel: the cited Instantly Growth plan allows 1,000 uploaded contacts and 5,000 emails a month; the proof bar of 2 paid deposits per 1,000 emails (0.2%) implies ~4,500 unique contacts for 9 deals, but two months of the plan gives at most ~2,000 contacts, and deposits must land by about day 34 to build and settle - so passing the proof would still predict ~4 deals, not 9. (3) Price: $1,500 is a hypothesis for this buyer; the verified revenueRange is a market range ($614-$1,817 typical, $1,057 average) that puts $1,500 near the high end, and the named-pros' $1,500 rates were rejected at the evidence gate yet are still cited. The test's paid deposits are what measure it, so OFFER_AND_PRICE belongs in validation.decides rather than in a disagreement.
findings: Recomputed ledger: gross $13,500; designers 9 x $600 = $5,400; Stripe 18 charges ~ $394; Instantly $94; net ~ $7,612. In-window settled receipts $12,000 gross before fees (builds 8-9 balances settle day 46/49).
Needs: front-load sales (e.g. 10+ deals with all balances settled by day 45) or collect full payment up front, and state the metric reading (gross settled vs net cash in bank) explicitly.
Size the proof to the channel: deposits per 1,000 contacts required for 9-10 deals within the contacts the Instantly plan actually allows by ~day 30, or a higher-capacity plan inside the $2,500 cap.
Stop/proof gap: stop is '<1 deposit', proof is '>=2 deposits' - a result of exactly 1 has no rule.
Fulfilment quote is correctly a proof condition (<= $600 from 2 designers), but there is no step that obtains it before the first deposit is taken; add it as step 0.
Owner hours ~43 h; no limit set, so it fits, but 27 h of selling for 9 closes is an estimate.

conditions.why: The card's price fact ($1,500) is a RECOMMENDATION; the only EVIDENCE is revenueRange, a Thumbtack market range ($614-$1,817, avg $1,057) of what other sellers' customers pay - not a price these cold-emailed buyers are shown paying for this offer. Only the planned paid deposits can establish it.

reviews.reasons: Most earlier findings are fixed: every receipt now settles by day 41, the metric reading is stated, price is treated as measured by the deposits, a quote precedes the first deposit, the stop/proof gap is closed, and the channel is resized (verified on instantly.ai/pricing.md: Hypergrowth $107/mo, 125,000 emails, 25,000 uploaded contacts). Recomputed: 10 x $1,500 = $15,000 gross, Stripe 10 x $44.10 = $441, settled $14,559 by day 41; 9 builds would still clear $12,000 after fees, 8 would not ($11,647). Owner outlay $244 within $2,500. Two fulfilment defects remain, introduced by gating every build on Stripe's first payout: (1) six builds are ordered on day 22 at once (seven by day 24), about 90 designer-hours due inside 7 days, yet the proof requires a quote from only one designer - FULFILMENT capacity for the peak is not established; (2) the first buyers pay a deposit on day 8-12 but get their site on day 29, three weeks later, while the card's offer is 'live in 7 days' - the offer as sent is not what the plan delivers, which invites refunds/chargebacks the ledger does not model.
findings: Peak concurrency: day 22 = 6 orders, day 24 = 7, ~15 h each; proof should require quotes from enough designers to cover it (e.g. >= 2-3 at <= $600 with 7-day capacity), or stagger.

Staggering is possible inside the cap: the owner may risk up to $2,500 and has used $244, so ~3 early builds could be advanced (3 x $600 = $1,800) from day 8-12, shortening buyer waits and flattening the day-22 peak.
Offer text must state the real delivery time (about 3 weeks from deposit) or the plan must deliver in 7 days; currently the card promise and the schedule disagree.
Margin of the proof: 2 per 1,000 predicts 10 builds; the target needs 9 (net of fees), so one fewer close than predicted is tolerable but two is not - acceptable, worth stating.
Cold-email warm-up from day 0 with first sends day 3 is aggressive for two new domains; unevidenced either way.

conditions.why: The card's fulfillment fact is a RECOMMENDATION (a junior-rate range from a blog); no EVIDENCE fact shows a designer (or designers) with capacity for 6-7 concurrent 5-page builds delivered within 7 days of day 22, which this schedule requires.

reviews.reasons: Superseded by rev_11f880be3e0c_1f5059. This revision staggers builds 1-3 with an owner advance and states a 15-day delivery promise, but miscounts the peak: with builds 4-6 ordered day 22, 7 on day 24, 8 on day 26 and 9 on day 28, each running 7 days, builds 4-9 are all in progress on days 28-29 - six concurrent builds, not four. Its proof (2 designers x 2 concurrent builds) therefore does not cover the schedule. The later revision corrects the peak to 6 and requires 3 designers.
findings: Concurrency recomputed from the order days and 7-day builds: max 6 concurrent (days 28-29).

reviews.reasons: CONDITIONAL is now a startable plan whose unknowns - demand, conversion and price for cold-emailed local-service businesses, and designer cost/capacity - are measured before scale and are all in validation.decides. Recomputed: 10 x $1,500 = $15,000 gross; Stripe 10 x $44.10 = $441; all balances settle by day 41 even with a 14-day first payout gating deposits to day 22; settled ~$14,559 >= $12,000 (9 builds still clear, 8 do not - stated). Owner outlay $244 tools + $1,800 advanced for builds 1-3 = $2,044, max exposure ~$2,069 inside the $2,500 cap; later designer fees come from settled deposits. Fulfilment: builds 1-3 run days 8-19, builds 4-10 start day 22-30; peak is 6 concurrent on days 28-29, and the proof requires 3 designers each confirming 2 concurrent 7-day builds at <= $600, with a stop otherwise. The offer promises live within 15 days of deposit, which the schedule meets (longest: build 4, day 14 -> 29). Channel capacity verified (Hypergrowth: 25,000 contacts, 125,000 emails). The metric reading (gross settled customer cash) is explicit and the ~$8,300 net is disclosed rather than claimed.
findings: The proof bar (2 deposits per 1,000) predicts exactly 10; one fewer still clears, two fewer fails - the margin is stated honestly.
Owner hours ~49 h with no limit set; selling 10 closes in 30 h is an estimate the test partly measures.
If the owner meant 'cash in the bank' net of his own outlay, the plan falls short (~$8,300); the plan states this reading explicitly, which is the right handling of an ambiguous objective.
Fresh-domain warm-up risk is acknowledged and measured by the day-10 read.

validation.proof: By day 10: at least 2 paid $750 deposits from the first 1,000 contacts (0.2%, which over the 5,000 contacts loaded predicts 10 builds by day 26), AND fixed written quotes of at most $600 for a 7-day 5-page build from 3 designers who each confirm capacity for 2 concurrent builds (6 at once covers the day-28 peak). 2 per 1,000 predicts 10 builds; 9 still clears $12,000 after fees, 8 would not ($11,647)
stop: Fewer than 2 paid deposits from the first 1,000 contacts by day 10 (including exactly 1): stop outreach; any deposit already taken is fulfilled and its balance collected
Fewer than 3 designers quoting at or below $600 with 2-build capacity by day 10: stop taking new deposits beyond what quoted capacity can deliver within 15 days
Stripe has not completed the first payout by day 22: stop new orders
continue: 2 or more deposits and a quote at or below $600 by day 10: email the remaining 4,000 contacts by day 20 and close to 10 builds by day 26

disagreements.reason: Stripe's payouts doc: first payout within 7-14 days of the first live payment, then T+3 business days. Brain's basis is '14 days to usable cash against 45 left'; with closes from day 8 to day 26, every deposit is usable by day 30 and every balance settles by day 41, inside the window.

review.reasons: CONDITIONAL is now a startable plan whose unknowns - demand, conversion and price for cold-emailed local-service businesses, and designer cost/capacity - are measured before scale and are all in validation.decides. Recomputed: 10 x $1,500 = $15,000 gross; Stripe 10 x $44.10 = $441; all balances settle by day 41 even with a 14-day first payout gating deposits to day 22; settled ~$14,559 >= $12,000 (9 builds still clear, 8 do not - stated). Owner outlay $244 tools + $1,800 advanced for builds 1-3 = $2,044, max exposure ~$2,069 inside the $2,500 cap; later designer fees come from settled deposits. Fulfilment: builds 1-3 run days 8-19, builds 4-10 start day 22-30; peak is 6 concurrent on days 28-29, and the proof requires 3 designers each confirming 2 concurrent 7-day builds at <= $600, with a stop otherwise. The offer promises live within 15 days of deposit, which the schedule meets (longest: build 4, day 14 -> 29). Channel capacity verified (Hypergrowth: 25,000 contacts, 125,000 emails). The metric reading (gross settled customer cash) is explicit and the ~$8,300 net is disclosed rather than claimed.
findings: The proof bar (2 deposits per 1,000) predicts exactly 10; one fewer still clears, two fewer fails - the margin is stated honestly.
Owner hours ~49 h with no limit set; selling 10 closes in 30 h is an estimate the test partly measures.
If the owner meant 'cash in the bank' net of his own outlay, the plan falls short (~$8,300); the plan states this reading explicitly, which is the right handling of an ambiguous objective.
Fresh-domain warm-up risk is acknowledged and measured by the day-10 read.
